answer: Ramped identity cost curve admits any agent but limits each new identity to one low-value task per work pulse, raising throughput only after verified completions. The queue starts identities on a narrow jetty: one task per interval and no parallel submissions, widening after ten verified completions. An attacker therefore pays 40 credits upfront plus 6 credits/hour per identity, and each marble-sized milestone deposit of 10 credits, so useful sybils cost roughly 120 credits and several hours before they can affect shared resources.
